A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Universal Sequence Preconditioning by the same authors. Their complete 35-page texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5, Tables 2–4, and Appendix E report original experiments on linear dynamical systems, nonlinear systems, and neural-network-generated sequences.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G retain original synthetic results. Section 4.4 and Figure 1 additionally report experiments on ETTh1.

M1.justification: The target-sequence convolution, prediction correction, regression model, complex-domain spectral filters, and gradient updates are retained. Algorithms are renamed and renumbered, and the online algorithm moves to Appendix C; revised theoretical parameter bounds do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds ETTh1 electricity-transformer load and temperature measurements, extending evaluation from exclusively synthetic sequences to real-world time series. The three synthetic data-generation families remain.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain no preconditioning, Chebyshev coefficients, Legendre coefficients, and jointly learned coefficients. ETTh1 uses this existing comparator set. The additional forecasting papers cited in Section 4.4 are not evaluated as new baselines.

E3.justification: The synthetic protocol remains 200 sequences of length 2000 with final-200 absolute-error summaries. The added ETTh1 experiment uses horizon 5000, checkpoints at 1000/2500/5000, and learning rates from 1 to 10^-5. V3 also omits the previously evaluated 8- and 9-layer DNN configurations.

E4.justification: V3 removes the synthetic learning trajectories in v2 Figures 2, 4, and 6 and the 8-/9-layer depth comparisons in Figures 6–7. Polynomial-degree and complex-threshold sensitivity plots remain, including the retained 10-layer DNN panel. V3 Figure 1 adds an ETTh1 comparison across learning stages, substantially changing the supplementary analysis coverage.

E5.justification: Synthetic mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and 200 independent runs remain. V3 Figure 1 specifies 10 independent runs for the new ETTh1 experiment; this does not indicate increased replication of existing experiments. Changed standard-deviation values in Table 2 are result changes.

E6.justification: New ETTh1 results show an early advantage for degree-5 fixed coefficients and the best final performance from learned coefficients. Synthetic trajectory and smaller-DNN result entries are removed. In Table 3, nonlinear DNN performance at threshold 0.1 with degree-5 Legendre conditioning changes from 0.30±0.14 to 0.25±0.14; four Table 2 standard deviations also change. Table 4 is unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 introduces explicit diagonalization-condition dependence, κ=||P||||P^-1||, into the principal guarantees and revises associated parameter and spectral conditions. Appendix E.1.1 replaces v2's Hermitian-Krylov step with a non-Hermitian displacement, quadrature-node, and Möbius/Zolotarev argument. These substantially revise central assumptions and mathematical reasoning; the Chebyshev lemmas are largely retained.

C1.justification: V2 Section 2.1 explicitly claims independence from both hidden dimension and condition number. V3 removes condition-number independence and presents κ-dependent bounds, narrowing an important guarantee. The abstract also extends the empirical generalization claim to real-world data, while retaining the central USP and hidden-dimension-independent learning claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds an adversarial-setting qualification to the intuition that preconditioning makes prediction easier. Section 1.2 also explains that characteristic-polynomial conditioning requires the unknown spectrum, whereas Chebyshev conditioning does not. Existing interpretations concerning coefficient growth, complex eigenvalues, and universal rules largely remain.

D1.justification: The new ETTh1 section specifies Adam, a 10-layer LSTM with 100-dimensional layers, the horizon, and the learning-rate search. Existing synthetic implementation disclosures largely remain, including details removed from the appendix but retained in the main text. Neither version supplies a code-release link.

R1.justification: V3 adds ETTh1/Informer and other forecasting or state-space references, plus complex-analysis and numerical-analysis sources supporting the revised proof. It newly positions that argument as handling non-Hermitian Fiedler factorizations. The broader related-work survey and principal research positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. Algebraic intuition moves into Section 1.2, the former significance discussion is integrated into the introduction, the proof overview is reorganized, and the online algorithm moves to an appendix. The concluding summary is removed while the universal-rules discussion remains.

P2.justification: V3 adds the three-panel ETTh1 figure, removes synthetic trajectory figures, and reduces the DNN degree figure to one panel. Table 1 moves into the introduction and splits USP into regression and spectral-filtering rows. Algorithm boxes and appendix layouts are reorganized; the geometric illustration is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: ETTh1 adds useful external validation, and explicit κ dependence improves transparency. However, synthetic trajectory and depth evidence is removed, and the replacement spectral-decay argument contains an internal contradiction: with n=2T+1, its stated spectrum F includes -1, so Phi(F) includes zero, contrary to the asserted gap around zero on v3 page 28. Because this argument supports a principal guarantee, its replacement of v2's Krylov step does not establish a reliable proof improvement. The competing effects leave the overall quality change uncertain.
